failures.text: How does an idea get from a draft all the way to paper trading with real allocated capital?
failures.answer: Sir, an idea climbs a fixed staircase: noted on a nightly card, drafted once its count how often it fires (for example the same miss on 3 of 7 sessions), registered when you say yes, then tested on 2000-2023 against the strict pass mark with 2024 onward kept sealed. Next it runs as a paper shadow book for 20 live sessions, and only if it beats random picks and the average stock on 10 separate sessions after costs, passes the check that no future data leaked in, and you say yes again, is it admitted so the allocated paper capital may use it. Real money needs one more step, the final real-money gate with your yes. Today nothing has been admitted: the stock rules and the options line are still in the shadow step, and no draft is waiting for you. One thing that isn't right, sir: the nightly replay has not finished since the night of 2026-11-14 (7 days ago); its never-again checks are that old; and 2 options trades scored this week at an entry more than 0.1% from the decision's own (the widest: BANKNIFTY on 2026-11-17, decided at 61,559.95, scored at 61,741.05, 181 points apart). Ask me what's wrong for the details.

problems.why: It uses terms a beginner would not follow, such as 'staircase', 'shadow book', 'never-again checks', 'the options line' and 'scored at an entry more than 0.1% from the decision's own', and none of them are explained.

results.answer: Sir, the biggest dated event is the RBI rate decision on Friday 4 Dec at about 10:00 IST, during the session, so it can move that day. Before that, India's GDP for July-September comes out Monday 30 Nov at 16:00 IST (after the close, so Tuesday 1 Dec is the first session that can trade it), and industrial production on Saturday 28 Nov. Abroad, the US jobs report is Friday 4 Dec (first Indian session Monday 7 Dec), the Fed decision lands Thursday 10 Dec at 00:30 IST, and US inflation on 10 Dec evening. Closer in, Bank Nifty's monthly expiry is Monday 23 Nov, moved up because Tuesday 24 Nov is a market holiday.

results.text: Ananta, how is the book doing?
results.answer: Which book do you mean, sir? 1. the practice book (the research trades). 2. my account on paper (the managed book). 3. the index options line.

results.text: Ananta, when do you ask me which one I mean?
results.answer: Sir, I ask only when a wrong guess would cost something: which draft to approve or skip, which book you mean, or what to flag when nothing came before it. It is always one short question with 2-4 choices, never for a plain fact question, and after one round your choice is the answer. In the last 7 days I did not need to ask you anything.
